verdict.rationale: Vercel automations such as Workflows and eve agents are shipped as code deployments, so the platform's Git-connected deployments, preview environments with comments, and instant rollback give them versioning, review, and rollback. The evidence documents this only at the general deployment level, not as automation-specific lifecycle management. Missing for 10: automation-specific version history and diffing, a documented review/approval flow for workflow or agent changes, explicit docs showing rollback of in-flight durable workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to deploy on every push, with a preview URL for every branch.
Let teams and invited collaborators comment on your preview and production environments.
Revert production to a previous deployment without a rebuild when something breaks.
Send a new deployment to a percentage of traffic first, then promote it or roll back.
Vercel Workflows runs multi-step logic as durable code that can retry failed steps, wait for external events, and resume across crashes and deployments.
